deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page belongs to Riemann's genus-3 theory: the 28 bitangents of a plane quartic and their expression through theta functions with half-integer characteristics. This is the material of his 1864 lecture 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen fuer den Fall p=3', published posthumously by Weber (Werke, 1876).

Notation.
- n, p, q, r and the fraktur letters d, e, f, g (the machine reads g as 'q' in many places) are characteristics, added mod 2.
- An expression such as 'n+p' names a characteristic. Odd characteristics label bitangents; for an odd one, the bitangent is the linear form sum_i (d theta_eps/dv_i)(0) x_i.
- A triple (a, b, c) of odd characteristics denotes the 3x3 determinant of the gradients of the three odd thetas at 0.
- theta_0(...) is an even theta constant.

1. Labels (top of page). Riemann lists the six odd characteristics n+p, n+q, n+r, n+q+r, n+p+r, n+p+q. He adds d, d+p and e, e+p. The forms x, y, z, xi, eta, zeta are the corresponding bitangents.

2. Cramer's rule, line e = ... (the '^2' is probably part of the label or a slip). The bitangent e is expanded in the basis x, y, z (= n+p, n+q, n+r). The basis forms are normalised so that d = x + y + z. Then
  e = (e,n+q,n+r)/(d,n+q,n+r) x + (n+p,e,n+r)/(n+p,d,n+r) y + (e,n+p+r,n+p+q)/(d,n+p+r,n+p+q) z.
The next line is the normalisation itself, i.e. Cramer's identity
  (n+p,n+q,n+r) d = (d,n+q,n+r)(n+p) + (n+p,d,n+r)(n+q) + (n+p,n+q,d)(n+r).
It is then compared with the analogous expansion of d in the second triple n+q+r, n+p+r, n+p+q, which gives a coefficient (d,n+p+r,n+p+q)/(n+q+r,n+p+r,n+p+q).

3. The coefficient alpha. A cross-ratio of determinants is set equal to a ratio of four even theta constants:
  alpha = sqrt[ (e,n+q,n+r)(d,n+p+r,n+p+q) / ((d,n+q,n+r)(e,n+p+q,n+p+r)) ]
        = theta0(n+d+f+p) theta0(n+d+g+p) / (theta0(n+e+f+p) theta0(n+e+g+p)).
Two intermediate forms are written. They agree with the final form exactly when the characteristics satisfy (my inference)
  d + e + f + g = p + q + r (mod 2).
This gives the identifications n+e+f+q+r = n+d+g+p, n+d+f+q+r = n+e+g+p, n+d+e+q+r = n+f+g+p, and so on. This alpha is the same alpha that opens the next page.

4. Companion coefficients.
  alpha'  = theta0(n+e+f+q+r) theta0(n+d+e+p) / (theta0(n+d+e+q+r) theta0(n+e+f+p))
  alpha'' = theta0(n+d+e+p) theta0(n+e+g+q+r) / (theta0(n+e+g+p) theta0(n+d+e+q+r)).
Riemann then derives
  alpha/alpha''          = theta0(n+d+g+p) theta0(n+f+g+p) / (theta0(n+e+f+p) theta0(n+d+e+p)),
  alpha alpha'/alpha''   = (theta0(n+d+g+p) / theta0(n+e+f+p))^2.
Both follow by direct cancellation once the mod-2 identifications are used (verified below). The side columns of characteristics are bookkeeping: lists of the theta constants occurring, checking which sums coincide.

5. Riemann's normal form. He writes the quartic as
  sqrt(x xi) + sqrt(y eta) + sqrt(z zeta) = 0
and begins writing the linear relation between x, y, z and xi, eta, zeta with theta-quotient coefficients, e.g. theta0(n+e+f+p)/theta0(n+e+f+q+r) x + ... = ... zeta + .... This is the programme carried out on the next page: x + y + z and alpha x + y/beta + z/gamma, each expressed by theta products.

6. The (d+p)^2 line and the Riemann–Jacobi-type quotient.
- The line (d+p)^2 = (d+p,n+p+r,n+p+q)(n+p)^3/(n+p,n+p+r,n+p+q) is a further normalisation of a bitangent coefficient.
- A double quotient of determinant products is evaluated as theta0(d+p+q+r)^2/theta0(d+q+r)^2.
- The relation (n+q+r,n+q,n+r)/(n+p,n+p+r,n+p+q) = theta0(n) uses the genus-3 Riemann–Jacobi derivative formula. That formula expresses the Jacobian of three odd thetas through a product of even theta constants; here it is used up to constants.
- A started expression (n+e) theta0(n+d+e+g) theta0(n+d+e+f) theta0(n+d+f+g) + (n+p)^2 ... is left unfinished.

7. Bottom: hyperelliptic characteristics. Riemann assigns half-period characteristics to the root functions sqrt((x-a_{2nu-1})/(x-a)) and sqrt((x-a_{2nu})/(x-a)). The upper row is (1)^{nu-1} then 0s; the lower row is (0)^{nu-1}, 1, (0)^{mu-nu}. This is the standard assignment of characteristics to branch points. The circled diagram (alpha, alpha_1', alpha_1'', alpha_1''', alpha_4) appears to be a sketch of a canonical cut/loop system.
errors: The second intermediate expression for alpha is garbled in the manuscript or transcription ('n+e+q+qr', 'theta0(n+d+f q)'). It should read theta0(n+d+g+p) theta0(n+e+g+q+r) / (theta0(n+e+g+p) theta0(n+d+f+q+r)) or equivalent; with the identifications this is consistent.
'e^2 =' at the top: the left side should be the linear form e itself (a Cramer expansion). The square is either a label/slip or a misreading.
The equalities for alpha, alpha/alpha'' and alpha alpha'/alpha'' are correct only under the unstated relation d+e+f+g = p+q+r (mod 2). This is implicit, not written on the page.

Determinant/theta identifications are used up to constant factors (powers of pi, signs) without comment. This is acceptable for projective coefficients, but signs of the square roots are left undetermined.

results.what: Expansion of a bitangent in a basis of three bitangents by Cramer's rule, with coefficients as ratios of 3x3 Jacobian determinants of odd theta functions
results.modern_name: Cramer's rule / linear relations among bitangents via theta gradients

results.what: Coefficients alpha, alpha', alpha'' of the Riemann model expressed as quotients of even theta constants; derived relations alpha/alpha'' and alpha alpha'/alpha'' = (theta0(n+d+g+p)/theta0(n+e+f+p))^2
results.modern_name: Theta-constant parametrization of the Riemann normal form of a plane quartic (Aronhold system)

results.what: Normal form sqrt(x xi) + sqrt(y eta) + sqrt(z zeta) = 0 of the plane quartic in six bitangents
results.modern_name: Riemann's model of a plane quartic

results.what: Determinant of three odd theta gradients proportional to a product of even theta constants
Characteristics of the hyperelliptic root functions sqrt((x-a_k)/(x-a))
results.modern_name: Assignment of half-period characteristics to branch points (Thomae-type)

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for Riemann's own published (posthumously, via Weber 1876) genus-3 theory: bitangents, Aronhold systems, and theta-constant coefficients of the form sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0. It is well known as his. Only the scratch details of the computation are new.

checkable.sympy: A,B,C,D,E,F=symbols('A B C D E F'); alpha=A*B/(C*E); alpha1=B*D/(F*C); alpha2=D*A/(E*F); simplify(alpha*alpha1/alpha2-(B/C)**2)==0
checkable.asserts: alpha alpha'/alpha'' = (theta0(n+d+g+p)/theta0(n+e+f+p))^2. Here A=th(n+d+f+p), B=th(n+d+g+p)=th(n+e+f+q+r), C=th(n+e+f+p), D=th(n+d+e+p), E=th(n+e+g+p), F=th(n+f+g+p)=th(n+d+e+q+r), and th(n+e+g+q+r)=th(n+d+f+p)=A, using d+e+f+g=p+q+r mod 2

transcription_corrections: Many symbols read as 'q' inside theta arguments are a fraktur g (fourth letter after d, e, f), e.g. theta0(n+d+g+p), theta0(n+e+g+q+r), theta0(d+g+p+q+r)? — compare the next page's alpha with 'n+d+q+p' = n+d+g+p.
The theta0(d+p+q+r)^2/theta0(d+q+r)^2 expression in the determinant-quotient line likely carries 'n+' and/or fraktur g; its first symbol is struck/unclear.
'e^2 =' at the top is probably 'e =' (the bitangent form), or the superscript is a stray mark.
In the hyperelliptic lines the characteristic notation is a two-row symbol (1 over 0)^{nu-1} ... (0 over 1)..., not a binomial coefficient.
